3F8eWL.name: Mixed Opalescent Colors
3F8eWL.description: Stringer Threads of glass pulled from re-melted Bullseye Compatible sheet. For use in kilnforming or torchworking. Stringers come in 0.5 mm (“Fine Line”), 1 mm, and 2 mm thicknesses and are approximately 17.75" (451 mm) long. They are packed in clear plastic tubes that are 18" (457 mm) long and 0.75" (19 mm) in diameter. Tubes are packaged by volume. A tube of .0.5 mm stringer contains approximately 350 pieces. A tube of 1 mm stringers contains approximately 123 pieces. A tube of 2 mm stringer contains approximately 50 pieces. Tubes of colors made with gold contain fewer stringers, to reduce unit price. For example, a tube of gold-bearing 1 mm stringers contains approximately 87 pieces, while a tube of 2 mm stringers contains approximately 33 pieces. Like our sheet glass, stringers are made by hand. There may be slight variation in color, thickness, length, etc.

2hC9hJ.name: Mixed Transparent Colors
2hC9hJ.description: Stringer Threads of glass pulled from re-melted Bullseye Compatible sheet. For use in kilnforming or torchworking. Stringers come in 0.5 mm (“Fine Line”), 1 mm, and 2 mm thicknesses and are approximately 17.75" (451 mm) long. They are packed in clear plastic tubes that are 18" (457 mm) long and 0.75" (19 mm) in diameter. Tubes are packaged by volume. A tube of .0.5 mm stringer contains approximately 350 pieces. A tube of 1 mm stringers contains approximately 123 pieces. A tube of 2 mm stringer contains approximately 50 pieces. Tubes of colors made with gold contain fewer stringers, to reduce unit price. For example, a tube of gold-bearing 1 mm stringers contains approximately 87 pieces, while a tube of 2 mm stringers contains approximately 33 pieces. Like our sheet glass, stringers are made by hand. There may be slight variation in color, thickness, length, etc.

3fPm9Z.name: Opaline Opalescent
3fPm9Z.description: The unique mix in this style will create a strong reaction and not reveal (or strike to) its target color until fired. Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

5tut61.name: Indigo Blue Opalescent
5tut61.description: Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

5UsgHY.name: White Opalescent
5UsgHY.description: Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

1DRaWL.name: White
1DRaWL.description: The unique mix in this style will create a strong reaction and not reveal (or strike to) its target color until fired. Limited Production Windows - Part of the fun and mystery of these styles is that no two are alike. Expect variation! To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

0yZ1eq.name: Almond Nugget
0yZ1eq.description: A light almond colored glass that when encased and using an oxidizing flame has inside veils of ambers to wispy blues but become more opaque with a reducing flame. Un-encased colors are lighter amber. Pulls thin, stays creamy, and nice for deep encasements.

0majKp.name: Cinnabar
0majKp.description: A striking color that is a dark shade of ruby. It develops its permanent color while working and doesn’t overstrike.

6Q0cGs.name: Cherry Brandy
6Q0cGs.description: An earthy red opaque color that strikes to multiple red hues. This creamy color is easy to work, but needs a neutral flame.

172Y8M.name: American Beauty
172Y8M.description: Gina Gaffner - "American Beauty is a beautiful deep dark red that can be thinned out with clear and can go along way and is super workable in all flames. This red will get super dark the longer you garage it in the kiln".

5r1t6y.name: Violet Hue
5r1t6y.description: It's a fun color to work with, because so many effects are possible. Working it slowly in a neutral to reducing atmosphere gives you hazy purples and greens and milky colors. Working fast in a hot, oxidizing environment gives you corals and raspberry reds, with some purple highlights.

63642S.name: Carmen Red
63642S.description: Gina Gaffner - "Carmen Red when worked on a a super cold flame (high oxygen) this color comes out beautifully. Another nice trick that I find with most cad colors is preheating them in the kiln before working them in the flame. Once cad colors are nice a warm you can typically get away with a hotter flame to get nice detail work done".

2bqm2A.name: Caribbean Coral
2bqm2A.description: This color produces a wonderful array of color swirls varying from salmon, corals, lavenders and purples. Work this glass hot with an oxidizing flame and the metals come out to play. Flame striking produces bolder colors.

4BsDM3.name: Charles Brown
4BsDM3.description: Transparent brown. This easy to use color has a smooth consistency and is great for sculpture and color blow outs.

4vfYvv.name: Encased Sunshine Yellow
4vfYvv.description: It’s covered with clear glass and you can use it inside or out without any problem.

0A62nF.name: Lemon Yellow
0A62nF.description: Lovely yellow color, resist boiling. Beautiful with slight translucency to it and is brilliantly easy to work. If it does boil on you a bit, just let that area cool and then dip in and out of the flame a few times. It is good is to use it as a base to lay stripes over it.

4HtEmj.name: Exotic Citrus Yellow
4HtEmj.description: A lemon color with some amber colors coming through. Blows out nice and easy. Friendly, easy strikingh.

38uuMS.name: Yellow Pearl
38uuMS.description: Gina Gaffner - "Yellow Pearl is a perfect color to layer over another to create organic texture. I love layering it with colors to create the juicy insides of many of my fruit and veggie pieces. This color seems to get a little darker when garaged in the kiln for a long time".

1N4VtL.name: Luminous Yellow
1N4VtL.description: Luminous yellow is like the early morning light on the volcano slopes of Maui, crisp, clear and bright.

2xHtp0.name: Orchard Plum
2xHtp0.description: This new multi-color has delightful amber-rose to plum with swirls of blue and silver. Very smooth consistency and good in all applications.

2hEKv8.name: Light Purple Haze
2hEKv8.description: A light transparent yellow with a purple haze which can develop a light white and yellow mix. A reducing flame will give the surface a metallic sheen. This color seems light from within.

5LdMLe.name: Exotic Citrus-Grapefruit
5LdMLe.description: Gina Gaffner - "Exotic Grapefruit Citrus is so organic I am able to use it for many fruits and veggies. I currently use it for my grapefruit pieces and my beets. The color works great in all flame types. A high propane flame will bring out the grapefruit color the most".

6adX16.name: Sunset Orange
6adX16.description: Gina Gaffner - "Sunset Orange hangs strong with the rest of the cadmium colors Momka's has to offer. Stable and easy to work with no worry of boiling. It is super dense as well".

4U0F6C.name: Challenge Gerber Orange
4U0F6C.description: Challenge series color with vivid orange stripes is easy to use and versatile.

5878nt.name: Challenge Gerber Pink
5878nt.description: Challenge series color, can be cut into murrini and has versatile uses. Gerber Pink can be struck to achieve deeper color; stable in deep encasements.

18Ydj7.name: Encased Carmen Red
18Ydj7.description: It’s covered with clear glass and you can use it inside or out without any problem.

1YgBdJ.name: Challenge Gerber Red
1YgBdJ.description: Challenge series color. Works well in deep encasements, but use a soft flame to avoid boiling. Like all the challenge series colors, this can be used as murrini, twisties, coil pots and the rest.

6dAGyJ.name: Palitra Orange
6dAGyJ.description: Each rod from Sunset Orange is covered separately with clear glass. Works easy inside or out.

4MhBwU.name: Challenge Sunflower
4MhBwU.description: Challenge series yellow color, can be cut into murrini and has great versatility. Pull into various sized stringer, even very thin stringer will hold its color and make beautiful flowers. Sunflower is stable, but needs to be worked cool in deep encasement to avoid bubbling.

0221Er.name: Greener Trails
0221Er.description: This multi-color rod has tones of green and amber-yellow shades all separated by clear. Favorite of bead makers.

3jPv2B.name: Brown Glitter
3jPv2B.description: This rich sparkly brown is very saturated and works smooth. Use a slightly reduced flame or oxidizing to neutral - melts & flows smoothly. The reflection of the sparkle will pick up adjacent colors. Don’t overwork or deep encase.

6ewzhC.name: Cobalt Blue
6ewzhC.description: One of the most appealing basic colors, is easy to work with and is little stiffer than other transparent colors. Cobalt can take lots of heat. Avoid reducing flame. Neutral flame works best.

75gzrR.name: Blue Flambé
75gzrR.description: Bright and lively blue and plays, beautifully as a surface color in sculpture. Work in a neutral flame, not too oxidizing for this one. Part of the beauty is in the haze that develops, yielding sky blues and purples and bright, royal blues. Generally develops beautifully just as it is works.

6BkcRG.name: Silky Satin Blue
6BkcRG.description: A very stable semi transparent blue with a touch of green that works easily in all flames. When encased has a light silky sheen.

04CDX0.name: Alaska Night
04CDX0.description: Blue-black striking color that changes into black, blue, gray, dark purple and bright blue. It’s wonderful in all applications. A fun color to work with that can develop silver reflective with a metallic sheen. Try this encased with a reducing flame.

2Uj5hC.name: Rainbow Blue
2Uj5hC.description: A dark blue glass with violet overtones. Work in a neutral flame and finish with a light reduction.

0wWLYc.name: Blue Lightning
0wWLYc.description: A cobalt based color which contains silver. This color strikes to opal with greens, blues and whites.

1nYGQN.name: Blue Treasure
1nYGQN.description: This multi-color glass offers blues and yellows that combine to make a wonderful murrini for flowers, jellyfish caps and realistic eyes that work best with a contrasting color. A myriad of color effects when deep encased. Experiment with this one; twisties, stringer, ghostly effects are all great. A favorite for ring making.

5Cnbz4.name: Crystal Blue
5Cnbz4.description: This is a beautiful transparent blue. Very clear blue and easy to use color. No boiling issues. Use an oxidizing flame, as you can get some slight red reductions with this glass.

5mwCVp.name: Forget-Me-Not
5mwCVp.description: Challenge series color with blue stripes and subtle yellow centers make fantastic murrini, twisties and wraps.

3N0nSX.name: Cloud
3N0nSX.description: Silver, gray and yellow light tones come through a clear base. Like the sun shining through after it rains.

2Sg1sS.name: Blue Reflection
2Sg1sS.description: Striking color with a light green, blue and purple.

5XZmPn.name: Violet Iris
5XZmPn.description: Transparent purple/violet with a lot less silver than Silver Iris. This is a great color for thick applications, sculptural work, and blow-outs.

2a5VaY.name: Magic Mirror
2a5VaY.description: Swirling honey with wisps of blue-purple and silver reflection. Blown out it tends to be a nice amber honey color. Outside work, with an oxidizing flame, gives a slight mirroring and iridescence.

3R7Hgg.name: Guacamole
3R7Hgg.description: A nice saturated opaque green. Less yellow than Martini olive. Use a gentle neutral flame.

2Z9HUQ.name: Ivy Green
2Z9HUQ.description: This is a beautiful rich opaque green. A true green, and very friendly.

2U8FzU.name: Martini Olive
2U8FzU.description: It is the lighter of our two opaque greens. Care must be taken to prevent boiling. Use a neutral flame.

1JhURV.name: Silver Pine
1JhURV.description: This is a nice opaque green with silver in it. You can achieve some lovely blue and green transparent luster's.

0Mztha.name: Sparkly Green
0Mztha.description: Smooth light transparent color with a lot of sparkling green. Work middle to cool flame. Slight oxidizing works best. Strikes with light tones to blue and yellow.

15Zu0z.name: Green Envy
15Zu0z.description: A very rich transparent green that develops faint wispy blue under strong oxidizing flame. Neutral flame to surface color tends to opacify while interior color surfaces develop a range of colors from tan to blue. Careful not to reduce, it will give an opaque red to exposed surfaces.

1HUU9q.name: Green Dragon 049
1HUU9q.description: Extremely smooth semi-transparent olive green sparkling green color with pearl essence. Start with a cool flame and then this glass can take any flame well. Not appropriate with deep encasing.

5nDju0.name: Silver Beach
5nDju0.description: A fast striking purple that is great for all applications. Oxidizing and neutral flames will give you dark purples, amber, yellows and blues. Silver Beach has stable color in deep encasement. Experimentation can yield surprising colors in pink, peach and green.

6kcjF4.name: Green Flambé
6kcjF4.description: This is one of our newest colors and is a green, blue silver color that works well in any flame and reduces well.

46MP6w.name: Silver Iris
46MP6w.description: Is a beautiful dark purple with lots of silver that is not affected by strong oxidizing / reduction flame. Get lovely blue/purple haze with annealing. The color intensity increases in larger work with more vivid colors. A popular color combo is Silver Iris and Magic Mirror.

13nZbG.name: Purple Thunder
13nZbG.description: This is a strong striking purple; very easy to strike. Beautiful pinks, rose, blue, creams and purples. Use an oxidizing flame. Best results are with some flame striking.

66GDKK.name: Violet Medley
66GDKK.description: An artist's favorite striking color. The rod is a funky avocado green and is worked like any amber purple by heating to white hot and keeping the surface haze burned off. When the piece is finished let it cool till the orange glow is gone and then strike to purples by reintroducing the piece to the outermost portion of the flame. Areas that have had the haze burned off will turn a rich dark transparent purple and areas that the haze is left on show up as a pretty cloudy blue. It is very easy to flame strike.

1d9x5C.name: Apache
1d9x5C.description: This multi-color glass is a whirl-wind of yellows, reds and oranges all separated by a bit of black. The colors are rich and intense. Easy to work and just screams out: wig-wag.

5ALnMa.name: Challenge Cherry Blossom
5ALnMa.description: Challenge series color with pinks, reds, ambers and white can strike to deeper reds; very versatile and easy to use.

3RhCPk.name: Gypsy Queen
3RhCPk.description: This multi-color glass reds, blues, greens, and white colors. This smooth and easy to work colorful rod offers new design options. Use cool flame if you want to keep the vivid colors.

4xhJKZ.name: Matador
4xhJKZ.description: This multi-color glass has two stripes of dark black, two stripes of red with thin separations of creamy white color. This bold color is easy to work and does best in a neutral flame; great in all applications.

2CT4fM.name: Marlee
2CT4fM.description: This multi-color is a classic. Red, Yellow and Green, all separated by Obsidian.

0k6t1L.name: Amethyst Ice
0k6t1L.description: This multi-color glass consists of two bands of plum harvest and two bands of a cream/white color. This color creates very unique effects in sculptural work; is great for quick canes for coil-pots and inside-out work. This rod makes detail very easy.

2RSx0p.name: Rhapsody in Blue
2RSx0p.description: This multi-color rod contains a symphony of cool hues of blues, emeralds and teals that dance and swirl through the rod. This glass works well inside and out, encased or not and makes a great twistie.

54aN0p.name: Infinity III -
54aN0p.description: This multi-color glass of vibrant blue and bright yellow is stable in deep encasements, and the yellow appears more lemony. Twisties can be pulled thin and the pattern remains clear. This glass works easily in all applications.

6t0NNY.name: Marlee II
6t0NNY.description: Multi-color rod of classic colors – red, gold and green separated by obsidian. Each of the colors is covered with clear to prevent cracking. Use a cool flame if you want to keep these vivid colors.

19HjNr.name: Infinity II (Coral Snake)
19HjNr.description: This multi-color glass has eight bands separated by clear. This one we playfully call coral snake. It is a yellow-dark blue-reddish combination that is easy to use and twists well.

3E6Rdt.name: Infinity
3E6Rdt.description: This multi-color glass has eight distinct bands of blues, reds, green and striking colors separated by clear. Easy to use, and makes a great twisty.

6E8rLV.name: Moonlight Sonata
6E8rLV.description: This multi-color rod has wonderful hues of blues, reds, whites and greens with a wispy pearly stripe. This glass works great in all applications. Moonlight Sonata makes a fast and beautiful cane when twisted.

19vBEq.name: Black Rose
19vBEq.description: An intense black with a dark rose violet undertone. Surface can get a little grey in heavy reducing atmosphere; recommend neutral to oxidizing flame. Black Rose is stable, durable and smooth. Thinning can result in transparent color.

31t7sV.name: Obsidian
31t7sV.description: A strong dark cobalt blue that does not thin out. Avoid reducing flame. Neutral flame works best.

2FjEGp.name: Black Bird
2FjEGp.description: Black rod with beautiful rich black tone. No reducing problems as long as you work is on an oxygen-rich flame. Stays bright and dense when worked in a deep encasement. It is non-transparent, non-reflective, our darkest and least transparent black. It is a darker black than our other black, Black Rose.

52YnKS.name: Bone
52YnKS.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Pastel test batch. Bone colored glass, can react with silver colors. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

1eZb8J.name: Violet
1eZb8J.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle violet pastel test batch. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

6Hq3f2.name: KRS-953 (1/4 lb)
6Hq3f2.description: Summary: Striking glass. Description: 2025 Test Batch KRS-953 is a silver and copper striking glass, a hybrid of Atlas2 and Skylla. .

53sL97.name: SKX-952 (1/4 lb)
53sL97.description: Summary: Striking glass. Description: 2025 Test Batch SKX-952 is a silver striking glass that can strike to a variety of colors. .

3pWfyw.name: SKX-951 (1/4 lb)
3pWfyw.description: Summary: Striking glass. Description: 2025 Test Batch SKX-951 is an experimental striking glass that can strike to a variety of blues and greens. .

0M2Jdx.description: Summary: Reduction Glass. Description: 2025 Test Batch ELX-942 is based on the retired color “Elektra”. Silver, golden, and iridescent lusters are possible depending on the type of reduction flame used.

6Uz9sL.name: THX-943 (1/4 lb)
6Uz9sL.description: Summary: Technical. Description: 2025 Test Batch THX-943, a variant of Theia, a transparent gold glass that produces blues and violets. Avoid overheating to maintain color.

58d1An.name: RX-940 (1/4 lb)

70TAGU.name: Zephyr 8 mm
70TAGU.description: Summary: Our non-reactive clear.. Description: Zephyr is a clear glass that has been formulated to melt smoothly and easily, resist boiling and scumming, have a low reactivity with silver lusters, exhibit a low seed count and have a pristine surface due to careful handling. Available in three diameters: 3 mm (2-4mm) 5 mm (4-6mm) 8 mm (6-9mm) Select your preferred diameter from the drop-down menu.

5DA1Z3.name: Hydros
5DA1Z3.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Hydros is a silver and copper glass creating an aquamarine color with a strong silver luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. To luster, work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

0h5aG9.name: Ananke
0h5aG9.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Ananke is a pure silver color that transmits a gold tone and develops a strong luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Ananke is a reduction color. Work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

6A6gaB.name: CLX-948 (1/4 lb)
6A6gaB.description: Summary: Reset, cool, then reduce.. Description: CLX-948 is color-shifting, reset-reduce glass, that transmits ambers and reds with the reds being more visible under incandescent and sunlight. It develops a strong silver luster and maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Reset-Reduce colors need to be reset in a neutral flame before following the reducing process. See our guide on how to reset. See our Phaeton Tutorial for the best techniques to use.

2E62nf.name: SRX-947 (1/4 lb)
2E62nf.description: Summary: Color-Shifting Reduction Glass. Description: 2025 Test Batch SRX-947 is a color shifting silver luster glass. The subtle blue green in sunlight shifts to full green under fluorescent light. An encased luster adds golds and yellows and an exterior luster gives a strong silver finish. .

6Dqpxf.name: CWP-794 (1/4 lb)
6Dqpxf.description: Summary: Technical Gold Glass. Description: CWP-794, a variant of Theia, a transparent gold glass that produces blues and violets. Avoid overheating to maintain color.

3wJSpD.name: Arke 2
3wJSpD.description: Summary: Reducing. Description: Arke 2 is our updated formula that increased the silver and improved rod quality. Arke 2 is a transparent cobalt luster color that develops a variety of exterior metallic finishes and holds it’s luster under a clear encasement. It’s the lightest of our three cobalt silver glasses; Arke 2, Triton and Iris. Variations in flame chemistry, exposure time and temperature alter the color of the exterior luster.

4ywjht.name: Atlas 2
4ywjht.description: Summary: Extra Strength Striking Glass. Description: Atlas 2 is formulated in our updated color base with the same nucleation system as our other striking colors. Atlas 2 is a highly saturated with silver as the only colorant. It can produce a range of colors both transparent and opaque, including ambers, purples, blues, and greens. It works well in both surface and encased applications. Atlas 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. It is very responsive to varied thermal history, allowing the development of many different colors on the same piece. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds cool/30 seconds strike. A clear encasement layer adds about 15 seconds to the cooling and striking times. Specific times and color outcomes will vary depending on several factors.

1nDNEK.name: Oracle Celadon Pastel
1nDNEK.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Celadon Pastel is made in our smooth melting Oracle White 2 base. 49BJwQ.name: Oracle ExtraBlack
49BJwQ.description: Summary: Oracle ExtraBlack; for best results, use a slightly oxidizing flame and avoid overheating.. Description: Oracle ExtraBlack has smooth working characteristics, reads dark even when pulled thin, and does not spread excessively. Oracle ExtraBlack is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. The goal of the Oracle project create is to create American made, low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle Black, Oracle White2, Rhea, Eros, Zephyr and Oracle ExtraBlack give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work.

5StWpn.name: Oracle White 2
5StWpn.description: Oracle White 2 is smoother melting than the original. It is our house white that we use in our murrini. 3Eh7YJ.name: Kronos 2023
3Eh7YJ.description: Summary: Reducing and opal glass. Description: Kronos 2023, is a blue silvered opal designed to replicate our retired color Kronos. Silvered Opals are R/T glasses. R= reduce. T = technical, in this case the T is for opacifying in the kiln., We recommend using moderately thin layers of the color and limiting annealing to 920°f for 1 hour to preserve the misty Opal effect. The pictured bead has a core of Kronos 2023 encased in Zephyr, with reduced Kronos 2023 scrollwork. .

2wzUNK.name: SR-880 (1/4 lb)
2wzUNK.description: Summary: Reduction Glass. Description: 2023 Test Batch SR-880 is a subtle aquamarine tint and a gentle luster give this reduction glass an attractive green-gold hue when worked. .

5m3VzE.name: ATX-890 (1/4 lb)

6Qeepy.name: Oracle Opal 2
6Qeepy.description: Summary: Technical Opal. Description: Oracle Opal 2 is a cleaner brighter formula than Oracle Opal. Oracle Opal 2 is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, Oracle Opal 2 will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. Further exposure to flame temperatures around 1000°F will cause more extensive opacification. For Best Results: Higher temperatures and longer annealing times can initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Bead: Zephyr core, layer of Oracle Opal 2, encased in Zephyr, with Oracle Opal 2 scroll-work The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame.

589YZ3.name: YP-861 (1/4 lb)
589YZ3.description: Summary: Reduction CFL Glass. Description: 2022 Test Batch YP-861 is a reduction glass that is yellow under natural lighting and pink/orange under fluorescent light (CFL). .

1d2DAN.name: DPX-832 (1/4 lb)

5N3LLN.name: Eros

4yuC3X.name: Hyperborea
4yuC3X.description: Summary: Reducing Glass. Description: Hyperborea has a rich violet and red color transmission and easily develops a strong silver luster when reduced. It works well both in surface applications and under encasement. The color is saturated and may present best over a core of clear glass, as pictured. A replacement to Boreas, Hyperborea is made in our updated color base resulting in cleaner colors, smoother working characteristics and improved viscosity curves. Based off of the BE test batches.

42SZCm.name: Okeanos 2
42SZCm.description: Summary: Dual; Strike or Reduce. Description: Okeanos 2 is a blue striking and reducing color. Reformulated with the same nucleation system as Terra 3 and Ekho 2, it strikes to a range of blues, greens, purples and amber. It works well on the surface or encased. Super-heating can cause phase separation, resulting in webbing. Okeanos 2 is capable of developing a subtle luster and retaining that luster under clear encasement. Okeanos 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds, cool/30 seconds, strike. Specific times and color outcomes vary depending on several factors.

4weppY.name: Ekho 2
4weppY.description: Summary: Striking and Reducing. Description: Ekho2 is a dual color, capable of both reducing and striking. It works best if you choose one technique or the other. Ekho2 is a reformulated version of Ekho. The nucleation system used in Skylla and Skiron has been added, resulting in a glass that is easier to strike. Ekho2 can be used as a surface luster, an encased pearlescent luster, struck on the surface, or struck under a thin encasement layer. The cooling and warming portions of the striking sequence for this glass are both approximately 45 seconds for the bead size and shape pictured. Specific times may vary depending on several factors. For best results in a striking application, apply a thin layer of clear glass to encase, then reset the Ekho2, cool, and strike the color through the clear. For detailed instructions, see our SnapGuide tutorial .

2bkurP.name: Lotis
2bkurP.description: Summary: Gold Pink.. Description: A pink version of Rhea. A lead free gold pink that plays well with silver colors and survives a reduction flame without discolorations. From test batch RO-682

6MfDv9.name: Rhea Light
6MfDv9.description: Summary: Pink gold ruby, technical glass. Description: A pinker version of our lead free gold ruby. Plays well with silver colors and survives a reduction flame without discoloration. Available by specific batch date. Odd lots are the unplanned result of a production run of a regular stock color. They are glasses that failed their color test because they were too dark, too light, or odd. We do not do color matching tests to make sure that one odd batch is the same as another odd batch.

0vN2GB.name: Phoebe
0vN2GB.description: Summary: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689.. Description: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689. See Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Hot Pink Bead with Rhea, Phoebe and Zephyr.

6A3w6r.name: Oracle Black
6A3w6r.description: Summary: Oracle-Black; Neutral with striking colors, reactive with lusters. Kiln-strikes to final opacity and tonality.. Description: Oracle-Black made in typical Double Helix fashion; with unconventional approaches to glass chemistry using low toxicity ingredients. Oracle-Black has smooth working characteristics, reads “darker” than some existing black glasses, does not spread excessively, and can be worked very hot without boiling. It is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Rods are dark blue but strike to black during the annealing cycle. Stays neutral with striking colors but reacts to luster colors. For maximum opacity, particularly in thin applications, briefly cool the bead then lightly flame strike (30 seconds) before annealing for 2 hours or more at 950F. The Oracle projec t is an extension of what we’ve already done with Aether, Zephyr and Rhea; create low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle-Black, Oracle-White (coming in 2018), Rhea, and Zephyr give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. Stunning. Buttery smooth to work, and the silver reactions are outstanding. Use with silver foil, or silver laden frit for absolutely fantastic effects.

1ec8L5.name: Skiron
1ec8L5.description: Summary: Skiron is our new silver-striking, rainbow glass.. Description: Skiron is our new, sliver-striking, rainbow glass. A major improvement over Luna 3 and Khaos, it resists over striking to khaki. Skiron works best when reset, cooled, and struck. Cooling and striking times will vary based on bead size, flame temperature, and other factors but general guidelines are; Surface applications: reset, cool for 30 seconds, strike for 30-45 seconds. Encased applications: encase, reset, cool for 45 seconds, strike for 45-60 seconds. The cooling cycle is an important factor in repeatable end results. Shorter than recommended cooling times typically yield white and purple, while longer cooling times can yield dark Amber with blue tints. Somewhere in between lies the ideal cooling/striking timing for your application and set up. Learn More View Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Skiron and Aether Bead.

20rHgF.name: Iris
20rHgF.description: Iris is the production version of the popular test batch AX-605. The A was for Arke and the X was for 10 times the strength! Though designed specifically for exterior applications, the silver portion of the luster will hold up under encasement. This reduction color can yield a multicolored metallic iridescent luster. Here’s a short video of the process. In our experience, a brush reduction flame produces the best results. Tips from Jed: It does require particular flame settings, and bead heat and reduction duration are more critical. My specific timings work for my specific set up. It is going to vary from person to person. Here is my process. 1) Shape bead 2) Allow bead to cool for 20 seconds. 3) Adjust flame so candles are stretched 2mm from neutral. 4) Pass bead through flame, candles should touch bead and deflect yellow flame around the edges. 1.5 seconds duration for each pass. 5) Allow bead to cool 5 seconds between passes. 6) Repeat pass-through and cooling cycle 5-15 times. 7) Anneal.

4wvZUU.name: Hyperion Light
4wvZUU.description: Summary: For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.. Description: A lighter version of Hyperion. Hyperion is a relative of Clio and our CX test series. A strong reduction color that is designed to strike automatically during the bead making process to medium amber. Encasing the light reduction in clear results in a purple pearlescent luster. For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.

6MwX4v.description: Summary: Speckled Luster. Description: Ossa is the first in our new speckled color family. Based on the popular “speckled luster” test batches OP-434 and OP-507. Ossa is a rich purple lustering glass with thousands of refractive inclusions dispersed throughout each rod. When exposed on the surface, Ossa can be left as a purple speckled glass, or it can be reduced to develop a variety of luster effects. Using variations in flame chemistry, Ossa can produce a solid silver metallic layer, or a multicolored iridescence. When reduced and encased, the inclusions in Ossa produce a textured mother-of-pearl effect reminiscent of some dichroic coatings.

1CCwRd.name: Aurae Light
1CCwRd.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Aurae light has the same silver-reduction strength as regular Aurae with a pink base color. Variations in the reduction process create mirrored, iridescent or satin textured lusters. If encased, the luster results in a pearlescent effect. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. For the satin textured luster, work in the tip of a larger reduction flame, let cool and then briefly reduce again until a subtle texture begins to form. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors. What are Odd Lots (Light, Dark, Odd) An Odd Lot is a batch of a regular stock color that did not pass its color matching test. If it was lighter than the standard, it’s labeled light. Darker, labeled Dark. For any other non color matching reason, it’s labeled Odd. Therfore, one batch of Light to another will not necessarily be the same. Some could be slightly lighter than the standard and others much lighter. A picture of the current batch of Light is in the gallery for your reference. 3zh71S.name: Oracle-804.AuOpl
3zh71S.description: Summary: Pink fast opal. Description: Oracle-804.AuOpl , a pink fast opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “fast” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it will develop substantial opacity when annealed at 920F. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for up to two hours. A translucent, opalescent strike will occur at these annealing temperatures. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Beads: the horizontal bead is a wigwag bead with Oracle-802.AuOpl and Zephyr. The vertical bead is a wigwag of Zephyr and cane of 802.AuOpl encased in Zephyr.

2DX9nT.name: Oracle-803.AuOpl
2DX9nT.description: Summary: purple slow opal, sold @ $60/pound. Description: Oracle-803.AuOpl , a purple slow opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to transparent pale purple. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “slow” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it may require very gentle flame striking or longer annealing times or higher annealing temperatures to develop substantial opacity. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for two hours or more. A translucent, opalescent strike can occur at annealing temperatures above 920F. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. The opal strike may also be initiated by resetting, cooling, and striking in a very cool flame before annealing. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-803.AuOpl+Zephyr cane and Zephyr encasement dots.

68Cfc1.name: Oracle-752.opl
68Cfc1.description: Summary: Was sold at $30/pound.. Description: 752.opl – An opal glass that strikes in the flame and kiln. Compared to the 740/743.opl it is slower striking, and more translucent after annealing. 752.opl can be worked hot and fast in the torch flame. Working notes: -To retain the transparent opal effect, limit kiln temperature and annealing time. I use 920F for up to two hours for misty-opal beads. Clear encasement seems to accelerate opacification in the annealer. Kilns vary in the amount of heat at the beads’ location vs the displayed temperature. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -A Reset/Cooling/Striking cycle can be used in the flame to alter the appearance of the opal effect. An encased bead that has been reset, air-cooled for 45 seconds, then very gently struck for 45 seconds seems to maintain the opalescent effect better than a bead annealed directing after resetting. The 752.opl’s reset and striking temperatures are lower than that of silver glasses. When reset, the glass is crystal clear, and when fully struck the glass is a milky opaque white. Variable opacity can be produced by controlling the thermal history of the workpiece. The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame.
