Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

36vtXA.name: Unicorn Tears
36vtXA.description: Unicorn Tears is a beautiful pink-purple with a touch of silver for a fumey effect. Working Tip: Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

1mrC1n.name: Tequila NoRise
1mrC1n.description: This is a Tequila color, without the reds and pinks that are Tequila Sunrise. Expect amber and yellows from this one. Working Tip: We recommend working in a neutral flame. Kiln strike.

5XERqq.name: Blue Satin
5XERqq.description: One of our classic colors. A royal blue color with a satin sheen.

1VC5KQ.name: Chocolate Opal (Dense)
1VC5KQ.description: A dense version of our Chocolate Opal, this color looks purple or brown in different lights.

0wHLxR.name: Chocolate Opal
0wHLxR.description: Chocolate Opal features many vibrant hues that shift in different light spectrums, from deep purple to brilliant brown.

66Kbge.name: Creme Brulee
66Kbge.description: A Creamy color that can be used in multiple applications.

2ud46c.name: Dark Wildberry Satin
2ud46c.description: Darker variety of Wildberry with satin chatoyancy. This shade is nice and dark when solid, and can be sleeved or thinned for a more transparent or translucent finish.

1UBeGS.name: Dense Glopal
1UBeGS.description: This is a odd batch of dense Glopal rod with a slight satin.

40YUk4.name: Dense Orange Opal (Unique)
40YUk4.description: This is a dense opal orange color with slight satin. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

2LwV7d.name: Dense Pineapple Juice
2LwV7d.description: This is a lovely dense cadmium yellow based color.

6CWKah.name: Dense Rose Quartz
6CWKah.description: Dense Rose Quartz is a dense version Rose Quartz with extra milky opal effect. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink.

0bcxBq.name: Diet Blue Cheese (Variant)
0bcxBq.description: This is a variant of our diet blue cheese. A lighter version of our classic blue cheese.

560JXE.name: Euro
560JXE.description: A clear that glows blue under UV.

1vkEPx.name: Exp. Black Pearl
1vkEPx.description: Experience the beauty of the Exp. Black Pearl Rod - a stunning, rod with an opalescent finish and a satin feel. Slowly pre heat rod and work it gently.

3yjEnH.name: Exp. Black
3yjEnH.description: Greasy Glass black rod. Our black consists of a super dense Wildberry variable. When thinned or exposed to bright backlight the color can show blue/purple. Keep dense for the most black affect.

25PMmP.name: Exp. Blood Orange
25PMmP.description: Vibrant transparent orange. There are some subtle variations in the strike from yellow to red and orange.

2jSSZD.name: Exp. Blood Red
2jSSZD.description: Bright yet deep toned transparent red rod that really pops.

1kYPUz.name: Exp. Blood Red (unique)
1kYPUz.description: Bright yet deep transparent red rod that really pops. This unique batch varies slightly in tone from the original, almost in the direction of a red orange though still definitely in the Blood Red family.

0RtMdv.name: Exp. Blue Phoenix
0RtMdv.description: A blue striking opal color that produces a range of hues from red to purple.

5TCTwA.name: Exp. Blueberry Opal
5TCTwA.description: This is a navy blue color in the same family as sonic.

6u0YhV.name: Exp. Bronze Pearl
6u0YhV.description: A Stunning experimental bronze colored extremely metallic looking color with opalescence to rival a pearl. Bronze Pearl shimmers and shines like a brilliant sparkle color, and also contains depth from the opal effect. This unique batch may have variations in color, and crystal size.

24nfhZ.name: Exp. Cinnabar
24nfhZ.description: A dense orange cadmium based color.

6Gz8Eh.name: Exp. Coral
6Gz8Eh.description: This is a cadmium based orange that looks similar to the marine invertebrates at the bottom of the sea.

0prpDY.name: Exp. Coraline Satin
0prpDY.description: Coraline Satin is a cadmium red satin color worked best in a gentle flame or encased. This is a limited batch available while supplies last.

0Y1JwE.name: Exp. Cosmos
0Y1JwE.description: A silver striking black that produces a range of colors.

2vbBhF.name: Exp. Dark Blue Raspberry
2vbBhF.description: Intriguing dark striking rod combining a medium saturation cobalt blue and a strong transparent ruby that strikes in the flame as well as the kiln.

43ZFB4.name: Exp. Dark Green Pearl
43ZFB4.description: Similar to Bronze Pearl, this Experimental Dark Green version appears dark and mysterious.

55gPt6.name: Exp. Dense Coral (variant)
55gPt6.description: This is similar to our coral but a little bit more opaque. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

0KAsbe.name: Exp. Dense Green Opal
0KAsbe.description: A cadmium based green opal that is a tad more dense than our Exp. Green Opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased. This is the only batch of Dense Green Opal from 2025.

0G5e6t.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal
0G5e6t.description: This is a vivid yellow with opal qualities. Color works best in a neutral to oxidizing flame or encased.

0sAqh2.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal (unique)
0sAqh2.description: This Exp. Dense Yellow Opal Rod is an ideal choice for a one-of-a-kind piece. Its unique mustard color and dense opal structure provide a visually striking effect.

0eSESf.name: Exp. Desert Rose
0eSESf.description: This is a cadmium-based orange with pinkish blush tones. Works best in a gentle flame or encased.

5D0f6y.name: Exp. Poofs (Dense)
5D0f6y.description: A cadmium based orange works best in neutral flame.

2juNZW.name: Exp. Green Olive
2juNZW.description: This is an experimental green color, best worked gently in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

4X3b3L.name: Exp. Green Opal (Dense)
4X3b3L.description: This is a one of our new green opal colors, this is a dense batch.

0epFXj.name: Exp. Green Opal (unique)
0epFXj.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased. This batch is slightly different than the original.

4KMD6w.name: Exp. Green Opal
4KMD6w.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

4F8M5D.name: Exp. Light Blue Crimson
4F8M5D.description: Exp. Light Blue Crimson is a flame striking red with a light blue cobalt base.

24zb5F.name: Exp. Light Orange Rainbow
24zb5F.description: This color can produce a range of colors. Samples were struck in the kiln at 1125 for a short amount of time.

2zbTjs.name: Exp. Orange
2zbTjs.description: A vivid semi transparent cadmium based orange.

0T4TkL.name: Exp. Pink Grapefruit
0T4TkL.description: This is an experimental orange/pink cadmium color with similarities to orange opal.

40utgY.name: Exp. Sonic Satin (Dense)
40utgY.description: Our classic sonic with a satin twist.

4VQuZH.name: Exp. Transparent Green
4VQuZH.description: An experimental transparent green. Best worked in an oxidizing flame or encased.

4AycB5.name: Exp. Yellow Opal
4AycB5.description: Our newest batch of yellow opal rod. A vivid cadmium yellow with opal qualities best worked in a soft flame or encased.

4YzvUs.name: Globalt
4YzvUs.description: Global is a light cobalt color that glows a strong blue under UV light.

1JA9fR.name: Glopal
1JA9fR.description: Glopal is an easy to work and stable opal with a pink UV glow. Milky opaque appearance to unworked tube, with UV glow and opal quality allowing for more or less transparency depending on working conditions. Use a hotter flame for more transparent finish and less heat for a more opaque final product. A thin layer of clear adds durability for higher temp flames and sculpting.

6T0Hv1.name: Gold Purple
6T0Hv1.description: A gold based purple opal color. Color needs to be full worked for purple to strike. To avoid hazing on gold colors work in neutral to oxidizing flame or encase.

6edTAb.name: Grease Stain (Light Strike)
6edTAb.description: A yellowish color with light silver striking characteristics.

6UeR8W.name: Green Energy (Light Strike)
6UeR8W.description: This is a silver striking green, you can get a range of color from due to the striking properties.

4yt2Pr.name: Ice Water (UV)
4yt2Pr.description: This icy looking transparent glows pink under blacklight. A subtle hint of satin creates the ice water effect, resulting in a standalone clear transparent, or as a component in building layered colored tubes.

0JKNpa.name: Icy Blue Satin
0JKNpa.description: A icy blue with a satin shimmer and Uv reactive.

0sdn8c.name: Jungle Juice (variant)
0sdn8c.description: Jungle Juice is a rich dark green color with sparkle effect. Work gently and does not like deep encasements.

6R1Ecc.name: Light Bright
6R1Ecc.description: A clear that glows Pink/Orange under Uv light.

3KqMrA.name: Light Olive Oil
3KqMrA.description: A transparent yellow with slight opal affect.

3ZFRHc.name: Light Phoenix
3ZFRHc.description: Light Phoenix appears as a bright and rich ruby red. Very similar shade of red as standard Phoenix with a finished appearance closer to a traditional ruby red than an opal version. This is a perfect option when seeking a true transparent red that shines bright. Light Phoenix may appear transparent clear when working and before annealing. For a faster strike, raise kiln temperature as high as 1100.

057YXL.name: Light Russet
057YXL.description: A light brown with a slit tint of orange.

1knuzg.name: Mango
1knuzg.description: Mango is a vibrant translucent yellow orange in the pineapple juice family. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

1aL44s.name: Marina (Dense)
1aL44s.description: A denser batch than our classic Marina. Works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

3zsy6L.name: Marina
3zsy6L.description: Crisp aquatic blue reminiscent of a clear pond on a bright summer day, Marina is a copper based opal blue. Marina is similar to and in the family of Hydro. Like all opal type colors, it will appear more transparent when worked hotter and more milky when worked cooler. This new batch is slightly more transparent than the last batch.

5u6uMJ.name: Moist Raspberry (Unique)
5u6uMJ.description: This Moist Raspberry (Unique) Rod adds a vibrant pop of color to any project with its flame striking ruby red hue.

4d7TX8.name: Moist Raspberry
4d7TX8.description: A striking red, for best results flame strike then kiln strike.

0t7akd.name: Neo Opal (Dense)
0t7akd.description: A more dense version of our classic Neo Opal.

4vPWGS.name: Neo Opal
4vPWGS.description: Our classic Neo Opal Rod a translucent purple color with opal properties.

2AnAFF.name: Opal Light
2AnAFF.description: Opal Light is a lighter variety of Gopal with the same working characteristics. It has less opal strike which makes this a good color for overlay variations.

3x7PuB.name: Peach Opal Agate
3x7PuB.description: Lovely pinkish opal color that verges into an occasional amber.

02nm58.name: Phoenix
02nm58.description: Phoenix is juicy opal red color in the range of ruby with flashes of purple. Phoenix can produce a range of colors depending on strike.

2Dw6ay.name: Pineapple
2Dw6ay.description: Pineapple is a light yellow cadmium color worked best in a gentle neutral flame.

6MfG4e.name: Pumpkin
6MfG4e.description: A cadmium based color in similar shade to that of a pumpkin.

5KCXeB.name: Purple Rainbow (unique)
5KCXeB.description: A unique Striking purple rainbow. Wonderful silver based striking effect in this transparent purple. Work this color using flame chemistry in between neutral and oxidizing to maintain transparency. Strike using a slightly reducing flame or by leaving to soak in the kiln. Note that raising the temperature of the kiln is not always necessary for striking purple rainbow. 1080F for 3 - 4 hours

4JUnwH.name: Rainbow Opal
4JUnwH.description: The Rainbow Opal Rod adds a unique level of color and shimmer in the flame with its opalescent rainbow color shift. It works in both oxidizing and neutral atmospheres and contains a combination of opal and cfl to maximize color enhancement. Its striking effects add a vibrant decorative touch to any glass design.

257hBT.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V12
257hBT.description: These rainbow sample packs are darker/dense opal colors. They contain two rods of each color, Dark Phoenix, Russet Opal, Yellow Opal Satin, Green Opal, Blueberry Opal, and Dense Neo Opal.

6XD7Y3.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V13
6XD7Y3.description: These rainbow sample packs have 2 rods of each of the following colors Dark Phoenix, Exp. Orange, Dense Yellow Opal, Green Opal, Sonic, and Dense Neo Opal.

64cMrK.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V14
64cMrK.description: These rainbow sample packs are 1lb 2oz and have 2 rods of each color. Transitional Phoenix, Exp. Coral, Exp. Dense Yellow Opal, Green Opal, Marina, and Neo Opal.

0q0mXb.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V15
0q0mXb.description: We have another installation of our Rainbow Sample packs. This version is 1lb 1oz and includes two rods of each color - Transitional Phoenix, Dense Orange Opal (unique), Exp. Yellow Opal, Exp. Green Opal, Marina, and Neo Opal.

0J6wT2.name: Rose Quartz (Transparent)
0J6wT2.description: Transparent Rose Quartz is a lovely intense transparent pink with CFL reactivity. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink.

0RgjHE.name: Rose Quartz
0RgjHE.description: Rose Quartz is a lovely transparent pink with slight opal effect. Under CFL it goes to a more intense pink.

5S909s.name: Russet Opal
5S909s.description: A light brown with opal qualities.

1TN2zc.name: Russet
1TN2zc.description: One of our newest browns added to the pallet. Works best in neutral flame.

2Adxdt.name: Shifty Peach Light Opal Satin
2Adxdt.description: Shifts from peach to pink under cfl, has a light opal and satin

63yUek.name: Smog
63yUek.description: A blue grey, with similarities to the hydro family with out the copper properties.

52wvgt.name: Sonic
52wvgt.description: Sonic is a rich blue opal. Similar in color to Dense Blue Cheese with an opal effect throughout.

3ZnbjR.name: Sparkle
3ZnbjR.description: Shiny metallic sparkle color. This is a great blingy sparkle rod in a classic gray metallic shade. Sparkle is a no-chrome metallic flake meaning it can be worked in any setting, surface or deep encasement.

2ebKg6.name: Striking Sample Pack V1
2ebKg6.description: This striking sample pack contains some of our striking colors. There are two rods of each color Light Moist Raspberry, Olive Oil Light, Grease Stain, Green Energy Light Strike, Transparent Gold Purple, and Cosmos.

04V7zY.name: Transitional Cinnabar
04V7zY.description: This is a semitransparent cadmium based orange, best worked in neutral to gentle oxidizing flames or encased.

3QdsVu.name: Transitional Mango
3QdsVu.description: Mango is a vibrant translucent yellow orange in the pineapple juice family. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased. This batch is more transparent then the last with a slight satin.

6adG8N.name: Transitional Phoenix
6adG8N.description: A red color with slight opal. This Phoenix is transitional due the amount of opal, it is in between Transparent Phoenix and Phoenix.

6B8xxx.name: Transitional Rose Quartz
6B8xxx.description: Rose Quartz is a lovely intense pink with CFL reactivity. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink. Transitional refers to the opal content of the color and represents the mid point between Rose Quartz and Transparent Rose Quartz.

59XMC4.name: Transparent Coral
59XMC4.description: This is a cadmium based semi transparent orange.

1jqfe8.name: Transparent Gold Purple
1jqfe8.description: A transparent royal purple. The purple in this color is brought out by fully working it in cycles of letting it cool down and reheating similar to working an opal color.

5fgs99.name: Transparent Gold Purple (Unique)
5fgs99.description: A unique version of our transparent gold purple rod. This is unique due to the saturation of gold in the color and the hue before being melted. To bring out purple color must be fully worked.

6nye5v.name: Transparent Marina
6nye5v.description: A transparent non opal version of marina. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames, or encased.

5CYb40.name: Transparent Phoenix
5CYb40.description: Transparent Phoenix appears as a bright and rich ruby red. Very similar shade of red as standard Phoenix with a finished appearance closer to a traditional ruby red than an opal version. This is a perfect option when seeking a true transparent red that shines bright. Color can produce more of an opal effect when encased.

5DXDV7.name: Transparent Shifty Peach Opal
5DXDV7.description: A transparent version of our shifty peach. Changes from peach to bright pink under cfl light.

305yrs.name: Transparent Shifty Sauce
305yrs.description: A transparent color that shifts from yellow to pink under CFL.

2m5kDV.name: Transparent Yellow Opal
2m5kDV.description: A yellow with light opal, use neutral flame for best results.

3uneEH.name: White Satin
3uneEH.description: Hand pulled creamy opaque white with brilliant satin and pink under UV light. Satin colors really shine when encased.

3DJCJq.name: Wildberry (variant)
3DJCJq.description: This Wildberry variant has a slight satin effect, and stays opaque when worked. Best results in a neutral/oxidizing flame.

3693eL.name: Wildberry Satin
3693eL.description: Pleasing variety of Wildberry with a nice satin content. Mostly translucent color that will appear closer to opaque if kept thick, and more transparent if thinned or stretched.

5Sm0kP.name: Yoshi (Milky)
5Sm0kP.description: Milky Yoshi, a staple of the Greasy collection. Clean and nearly opaque with a strong CFL shift. This is B grade due to streaks.Easy to work. Preheat tubing slowly in kiln to avoid cracking.

0eEa65.name: Yoshi
0eEa65.description: Yoshi, a staple of the Greasy Glass collection. A vibrant green that shifts pink under CFL light.

5DA1Z4.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Hydros is a silver and copper glass creating an aquamarine color with a strong silver luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. To luster, work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

0h5aGA.name: Ananke
0h5aGA.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Ananke is a pure silver color that transmits a gold tone and develops a strong luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Ananke is a reduction color. Work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

3wJSpE.name: Arke 2
3wJSpE.description: Summary: Reducing. Description: Arke 2 is our updated formula that increased the silver and improved rod quality. Arke 2 is a transparent cobalt luster color that develops a variety of exterior metallic finishes and holds it’s luster under a clear encasement. It’s the lightest of our three cobalt silver glasses; Arke 2, Triton and Iris. Variations in flame chemistry, exposure time and temperature alter the color of the exterior luster.

4ywjhu.name: Atlas 2
4ywjhu.description: Summary: Extra Strength Striking Glass. Description: Atlas 2 is formulated in our updated color base with the same nucleation system as our other striking colors. Atlas 2 is a highly saturated with silver as the only colorant. It can produce a range of colors both transparent and opaque, including ambers, purples, blues, and greens. It works well in both surface and encased applications. Atlas 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. It is very responsive to varied thermal history, allowing the development of many different colors on the same piece. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds cool/30 seconds strike. A clear encasement layer adds about 15 seconds to the cooling and striking times. Specific times and color outcomes will vary depending on several factors.

1nDNEL.name: Oracle Celadon Pastel
1nDNEL.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Celadon Pastel is made in our smooth melting Oracle White 2 base. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

0jJL8D.name: Oracle Lapis
0jJL8D.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Lapis is a rich cobalt blue opaque made in our smooth melting Oracle White 2 base glass. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

49BJwR.name: Oracle ExtraBlack
49BJwR.description: Summary: Oracle ExtraBlack; for best results, use a slightly oxidizing flame and avoid overheating.. Description: Oracle ExtraBlack has smooth working characteristics, reads dark even when pulled thin, and does not spread excessively. Oracle ExtraBlack is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. The goal of the Oracle project create is to create American made, low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle Black, Oracle White2, Rhea, Eros, Zephyr and Oracle ExtraBlack give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work.

5StWpp.name: Oracle White 2

2sUwzX.name: Oracle Pink Pastel
2sUwzX.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Pink Pastel is a nearly opaque glass that requires no special treatment to develop its smooth and consistent soft pink tone. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

6UKeGv.name: Elpis 2
6UKeGv.description: Summary: Reducing Glass. Description: Elpis 2 is made in our updated color base resulting in cleaner colors, smoother working characteristics and improved viscosity curves. Elpis 2 is a chrome-free green reducing glass that transmits a spring green color and is resistant to over reducing. Based on test batch PX-772.

6Qeepz.name: Oracle Opal 2
6Qeepz.description: Summary: Technical Opal. Description: Oracle Opal 2 is a cleaner brighter formula than Oracle Opal. Oracle Opal 2 is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, Oracle Opal 2 will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. Further exposure to flame temperatures around 1000°F will cause more extensive opacification. For Best Results: Higher temperatures and longer annealing times can initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Bead: Zephyr core, layer of Oracle Opal 2, encased in Zephyr, with Oracle Opal 2 scroll-work The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame.

5N3LLP.name: Eros
5N3LLP.description: Summary: Technical Glass. Description: Eros, our gold-pink. Based on test batch HWP-791 and Rhea Light. Avoid overheating to maintain color. The Lighter Bead: is Eros sandwiched between layers of Zephyr with Eros scroll work. The Darker Bead: a core of Eros encased in Zephyr with Eros scroll work.

4yuC3Y.name: Hyperborea
4yuC3Y.description: Summary: Reducing Glass. Description: Hyperborea has a rich violet and red color transmission and easily develops a strong silver luster when reduced. It works well both in surface applications and under encasement. The color is saturated and may present best over a core of clear glass, as pictured. A replacement to Boreas, Hyperborea is made in our updated color base resulting in cleaner colors, smoother working characteristics and improved viscosity curves. Based off of the BE test batches.

42SZCn.name: Okeanos 2
42SZCn.description: Summary: Dual; Strike or Reduce. Description: Okeanos 2 is a blue striking and reducing color. Reformulated with the same nucleation system as Terra 3 and Ekho 2, it strikes to a range of blues, greens, purples and amber. It works well on the surface or encased. Super-heating can cause phase separation, resulting in webbing. Okeanos 2 is capable of developing a subtle luster and retaining that luster under clear encasement. Okeanos 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds, cool/30 seconds, strike. Specific times and color outcomes vary depending on several factors.

4weppZ.name: Ekho 2
4weppZ.description: Summary: Striking and Reducing. Description: Ekho2 is a dual color, capable of both reducing and striking. It works best if you choose one technique or the other. Ekho2 is a reformulated version of Ekho. The nucleation system used in Skylla and Skiron has been added, resulting in a glass that is easier to strike. Ekho2 can be used as a surface luster, an encased pearlescent luster, struck on the surface, or struck under a thin encasement layer. The cooling and warming portions of the striking sequence for this glass are both approximately 45 seconds for the bead size and shape pictured. Specific times may vary depending on several factors. For best results in a striking application, apply a thin layer of clear glass to encase, then reset the Ekho2, cool, and strike the color through the clear. For detailed instructions, see our SnapGuide tutorial .

0vN2GC.name: Phoebe
0vN2GC.description: Summary: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689.. Description: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689. See Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Hot Pink Bead with Rhea, Phoebe and Zephyr.

2bkurQ.name: Lotis
2bkurQ.description: Summary: Gold Pink.. Description: A pink version of Rhea. A lead free gold pink that plays well with silver colors and survives a reduction flame without discolorations. From test batch RO-682

6A3w6u.name: Oracle Black
6A3w6u.description: Summary: Oracle-Black; Neutral with striking colors, reactive with lusters. Kiln-strikes to final opacity and tonality.. Description: Oracle-Black made in typical Double Helix fashion; with unconventional approaches to glass chemistry using low toxicity ingredients. Oracle-Black has smooth working characteristics, reads “darker” than some existing black glasses, does not spread excessively, and can be worked very hot without boiling. It is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Rods are dark blue but strike to black during the annealing cycle. Stays neutral with striking colors but reacts to luster colors. For maximum opacity, particularly in thin applications, briefly cool the bead then lightly flame strike (30 seconds) before annealing for 2 hours or more at 950F. The Oracle projec t is an extension of what we’ve already done with Aether, Zephyr and Rhea; create low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle-Black, Oracle-White (coming in 2018), Rhea, and Zephyr give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. Stunning. Buttery smooth to work, and the silver reactions are outstanding. Use with silver foil, or silver laden frit for absolutely fantastic effects.

1ec8L6.name: Skiron
1ec8L6.description: Summary: Skiron is our new silver-striking, rainbow glass.. Description: Skiron is our new, sliver-striking, rainbow glass. A major improvement over Luna 3 and Khaos, it resists over striking to khaki. Skiron works best when reset, cooled, and struck. Cooling and striking times will vary based on bead size, flame temperature, and other factors but general guidelines are; Surface applications: reset, cool for 30 seconds, strike for 30-45 seconds. Encased applications: encase, reset, cool for 45 seconds, strike for 45-60 seconds. The cooling cycle is an important factor in repeatable end results. Shorter than recommended cooling times typically yield white and purple, while longer cooling times can yield dark Amber with blue tints. Somewhere in between lies the ideal cooling/striking timing for your application and set up. Learn More View Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Skiron and Aether Bead.

20rHgG.name: Iris
20rHgG.description: Iris is the production version of the popular test batch AX-605. The A was for Arke and the X was for 10 times the strength! Though designed specifically for exterior applications, the silver portion of the luster will hold up under encasement. This reduction color can yield a multicolored metallic iridescent luster. Here’s a short video of the process. In our experience, a brush reduction flame produces the best results. Tips from Jed: It does require particular flame settings, and bead heat and reduction duration are more critical. My specific timings work for my specific set up. It is going to vary from person to person. Here is my process. 1) Shape bead 2) Allow bead to cool for 20 seconds. 3) Adjust flame so candles are stretched 2mm from neutral. 4) Pass bead through flame, candles should touch bead and deflect yellow flame around the edges. 1.5 seconds duration for each pass. 5) Allow bead to cool 5 seconds between passes. 6) Repeat pass-through and cooling cycle 5-15 times. 7) Anneal.

3w2NwQ.name: Hyperion
3w2NwQ.description: Summary: For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.. Description: Hyperion is a relative of Clio and our CX test series. A strong reduction color that is designed to strike automatically during the bead making process to medium amber. Encasing the light reduction in clear results in a purple pearlescent luster. For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.

6MwX4w.name: Ossa
6MwX4w.description: Summary: Speckled Luster. Description: Ossa is the first in our new speckled color family. Based on the popular “speckled luster” test batches OP-434 and OP-507. Ossa is a rich purple lustering glass with thousands of refractive inclusions dispersed throughout each rod. When exposed on the surface, Ossa can be left as a purple speckled glass, or it can be reduced to develop a variety of luster effects. Using variations in flame chemistry, Ossa can produce a solid silver metallic layer, or a multicolored iridescence. When reduced and encased, the inclusions in Ossa produce a textured mother-of-pearl effect reminiscent of some dichroic coatings.

5VWjK8.name: Kalypso
5VWjK8.description: Summary: Striking and reducing. Description: Kalypso is more intense and saturated version of Clio. It’s a color-shifting, reset-reduce glass, that transmits ambers and reds with the reds being more visible under incandescent and sunlight. It develops a strong silver luster and maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Reset-Reduce colors need to be reset in a neutral flame before following the reducing process. See our guide on how to reset. See our Phaeton Tutorial for the best techniques to use with Clio. Based of of test batches NE-323, KA-356 and KA-357. WONDERFUL….. It is so easy to get the most amazing colors out of this glass. Simply stunning! I LOVE THIS COLOR I love pink and purple especially but this color is very easy to strike and work with. I am so glad it exists. Please keep up the outstanding work and coming up with such amazing colors for us.

1CCwRg.name: Aurae Light
1CCwRg.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Aurae light has the same silver-reduction strength as regular Aurae with a pink base color. Variations in the reduction process create mirrored, iridescent or satin textured lusters. If encased, the luster results in a pearlescent effect. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. For the satin textured luster, work in the tip of a larger reduction flame, let cool and then briefly reduce again until a subtle texture begins to form. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors. What are Odd Lots (Light, Dark, Odd) An Odd Lot is a batch of a regular stock color that did not pass its color matching test. If it was lighter than the standard, it’s labeled light. Darker, labeled Dark. For any other non color matching reason, it’s labeled Odd. Therfore, one batch of Light to another will not necessarily be the same. Some could be slightly lighter than the standard and others much lighter. A picture of the current batch of Light is in the gallery for your reference. 2DX9nU.description: Summary: purple slow opal, sold @ $60/pound. Description: Oracle-803.AuOpl , a purple slow opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to transparent pale purple. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “slow” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it may require very gentle flame striking or longer annealing times or higher annealing temperatures to develop substantial opacity. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for two hours or more. A translucent, opalescent strike can occur at annealing temperatures above 920F. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. The opal strike may also be initiated by resetting, cooling, and striking in a very cool flame before annealing. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-803.AuOpl+Zephyr cane and Zephyr encasement dots.

This opal is “fast” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it will develop substantial opacity when annealed at 920F. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for up to two hours. A translucent, opalescent strike will occur at these annealing temperatures. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Beads: the horizontal bead is a wigwag bead with Oracle-802.AuOpl and Zephyr. 68Cfc2.description: Summary: Was sold at $30/pound.. Description: 752.opl – An opal glass that strikes in the flame and kiln. Compared to the 740/743.opl it is slower striking, and more translucent after annealing. 752.opl can be worked hot and fast in the torch flame. Working notes: -To retain the transparent opal effect, limit kiln temperature and annealing time. I use 920F for up to two hours for misty-opal beads. Clear encasement seems to accelerate opacification in the annealer. Kilns vary in the amount of heat at the beads’ location vs the displayed temperature. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -A Reset/Cooling/Striking cycle can be used in the flame to alter the appearance of the opal effect. An encased bead that has been reset, air-cooled for 45 seconds, then very gently struck for 45 seconds seems to maintain the opalescent effect better than a bead annealed directing after resetting. The 752.opl’s reset and striking temperatures are lower than that of silver glasses. When reset, the glass is crystal clear, and when fully struck the glass is a milky opaque white. Variable opacity can be produced by controlling the thermal history of the workpiece. The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame. The Oracle Project Test Batches – offered direct from the glassmaker to the artisan in small batches, sold by the pound, wrapped in paper. Labeled with batch date and formula number, with a suffix to indicate glass family type example, 740.opl

0LGWAc.name: Oracle-780.vopl
0LGWAc.description: Summary: Slow Violet Opal. Description: 780.vopl is a violet tinted slow opal that opacifies in the flame and kiln. When reset, the glass is transparent violet, and when fully struck the glass is an opaque lavender color. Areas that have started to opacify in the flame will continue to opacify in the annealer. Striking temperatures are lower than that of our silver glasses. Working notes: This slow opal stays mostly reset during many beadmaking operations, and can strike to a misty-opal or opaque lavender color during annealing. I anneal this color at 975°F for up to five hours for semi-opaque beads, depending on size, encasement, and other factors. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks
